s10.old: - **Refinement (user feedback):** the user noted "Neutral" was mislabeling members who HAVE worked with CUs (Fitzpatrick etc.); it only meant *light positive lean* (D below the Ally cutoff). Fix: (1) lowered **Ally cutoff 0.0575 to 0.034** (`RA!L8` dial; 77 members Neutral to Ally; Fitzpatrick/Young Kim/Crapo/De La Cruz now Ally; allocation unchanged, stance is allocation-independent). (2) Split persuadables into **Flip-Neutral** (connected-but-uncommitted: Ritchie Torres, Cortez Masto, Beatty, Brad Sherman, Susan Collins), **Flip-Skeptic** (truly persuadable skeptics: Warnock, Aaron Bean, **John Boozman**, who heavily co-sponsors with pro-CU) and **Solidify** (newly-recognized soft allies to lock in: Fitzpatrick, De La Cruz, Young Kim), each ranked by within-group z(pro_pull)+z(centrality)+z(frustration). (3) **Bug fixed:** `pro_pull` must use UNSIGNED collaboration magnitude to pro-camp (skeptic-to-pro edges are signed negative, so the old `sw>0` filter zeroed every skeptic's reachability). The threshold and split are tunable dials = user's call.

s10.old: - **Adaptive backbone = Golovin & Krause "Adaptive Submodularity" (JAIR 2011, in Downloads).** Fund a member, observe persuaded/who-they-bring, adaptively pick next. Adaptive-greedy = (1-1/e) of optimal policy when the objective is adaptive-monotone + adaptive-submodular; alpha-approx greedy gives (1-1/e^{1/α}); the cost-sensitive version maps the $ budget to per-member costs c(e). Adaptive IM (coalition/ICM mode) IS adaptive submodular, so a clean guarantee; competitive-LT flip mode is generally NOT, so OR-model/heuristic path.
s10.why: "adaptively pick next" is the algorithm's sequence

s10.old: - **PER-CONFIG NODE LAYOUTS @b9ff46982** (Paul: "Option 1, with the animated transition", reversing the earlier fixed-position choice). Each config now carries its own force layout and the field animates 600 ms between them. **THE HARD PART WAS THE COORDINATE FRAME, NOT THE ANIMATION** (generalizes to any visual comparison of two computed embeddings). A force layout is rotation/reflection invariant and `spring_layout` ends with `rescale_layout()` (normalizes every layout to max|coord|=1 about its OWN centroid), so orientation and absolute size are pure gauge. Rendering three independently computed, independently min/max-scaled layouts would animate that gauge as if it were structure: measured, naive = median shift **224** canvas units with corr(CU) 0.45/0.39, vs shipped = **75** with 0.58/0.69. **Two thirds of the naive movement was frame artifact.** Fix = (1) warm-start each layout from the published CU canvas so the solver lands in the NEAREST minimum, (2) Procrustes-align back onto CU (rotation + reflection + uniform scale + translation; reflection ALLOWED, no handedness to protect), (3) NO per-layout rescaler. Plus `k_cfg = 0.45*(mean_w_cfg/mean_w_CU)^(1/3)`, from the FR energy's invariance under (A,k) to (cA, c^(1/3) k), so unrelated weight units cannot masquerade as layout change. Committee layout is EXEMPT (its coords come from workbook membership; anchor labels are drawn at fixed points). Side effect: **repaired a latent bug**: area layout rebuilt PE on config change but never respaced, so lines were weighted by the new kernel over the old embedding while the caption claimed otherwise; median move 0 to 374. Party structure is STRONGER in the new layouts (1-NN same-party .936 holistic / .908 norm vs .783 CU), so the movement is signal.
s10.why: "reversing the earlier fixed-position choice" is time

s10.old: - **THIRD UNINTENDED PRODUCTION WRITE OF THE SESSION, same root cause: `import == execution`.** Importing the augmenter merely to TEST its config guard wrote `holistic_network_AUG_20260819.xlsx`. Content-identical to the reviewed artifact (63,707 rows, canonical sha a437dd6d) but newest-by-mtime had already made it the graph the engine would load. Moved to `backups/accidental_20260819/`, NOT deleted; selection verified back on 20260818. **Three occurrences means resolutions do not work; the fix is STRUCTURAL: `NET_VALIDATE_ONLY=1` exits after the config verdict and writes nothing (42 xlsx before and after).** A guard you cannot exercise without side effects is a guard nobody will exercise. Its own negative control then caught that I had put the early exit ABOVE the sector refusal, so sectors reported ACCEPTED: **order your early exits after your refusals, and always negative-control a guard.**
